title: prefill/decoding: chunked speculative prefill + stage overlap scheduling optimizations
author: Evan Lin
description:
Motivation: reduce end-to-end latency and increase throughput for mixed prefill+decode workloads (chat, streaming) by overlapping prefill and decode stages, introducing chunked prefill paths to avoid large tensor allocations, and enabling speculative prefill for short-prefill long-decode patterns. This PR implements a scheduling model that: 1) splits long prefill sequences into configurable chunks to allow earlier KV cache availability; 2) schedules decode work opportunistically while later prefill chunks are still running (stage overlap); and 3) uses a lightweight speculative prefill path for requests where decoding is likely to proceed immediately (based on request heuristics and historical telemetry).

Summary of changes: added chunked prefill execution in the runtime, new scheduler heuristics to allow prefill/decode stage overlap, a speculative prefill codepath that performs a trimmed prefill to prime KV caches and early kernels, and kernel-level tweaks to make attention and KV read/write safer under concurrent access. Also includes feature flags and rolling metrics hooks for safe rollout.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-4123) linked and reviewed
- [x] Microbenchmarks showing throughput/latency gains
- [x] End-to-end regression tests
- [x] Observability/metric hooks added
- [x] Feature-flagged rollout

Design notes and decisions: chunking size defaults to 128 tokens (configurable per model profile). Chunked prefill reduces peak memory footprint and allows earlier KV availability; this is particularly beneficial for long-context models where prefill dominates. Stage overlap scheduling is conservative by default: we only start decode when the first prefill chunk and its KV flush complete; further chunks continue in parallel on separate workers or streams. Speculative prefill is gated behind a flag and uses a heuristic based on (request.size, historical decode probability) to avoid wasted work for pure embeddings/analysis requests. Kernel changes add epoch-based KV version checks to ensure correctness when overlapped reads/writes occur.

Benchmarks (representative):
- Latency p95 for chat workload (prefill 1024 tokens + decode 64 tokens): p95 reduced from 280ms -> 220ms (approx 21% drop).
- Throughput for throughput-bound batch (batch size 8, seq=512): +12% tokens/s improvement in mixed workloads.
- Memory peak on 80B model reduced ~9% for long prefills due to chunking.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to dedicated pools, gradual percent rollout with metrics guardrails (p95 latency, error rate, kv-mismatch alerts). If regressions are detected we will automatically disable speculative prefill and fall back to safe single-shot prefill.

Related: Linear ENG-4123, ENG-4219; perf canary tickets PERF-178, PERF-201. See docs: docs/perf/prefill_decode_overlap.md.

ci_details: Initial presubmit had one flaky perf test (prefill_overlap_canary) failing under heavy contention; test re-run passed. Integration and GPU nightly passed. Lint and typechecks passed.
release_notes:
- Introduces chunked prefill execution to reduce peak memory and allow earlier KV availability.
- Adds stage-overlap scheduler to overlap prefill and decode stages for lower p95 latency.
- Implements speculative prefill feature-flag to prime KV for likely-decode requests (off by default).
- Kernel-level safety checks for concurrent KV access.
- Performance improvements: ~12% throughput, up to 21% p95 latency reduction in representative chat workloads.
review_comments: Aisha Khan (review): Please add a short-circuit path for pure-embedding requests (no decode) so we don't do speculative work. Author: added heuristic gate and unit tests.

Diego Martinez (review): The KV epoch checks look correct but we need stronger asserts in debug builds to catch races. Author: added debug-only asserts and an integration test that injects artificial delays.
Priya Patel (review): Can we make chunk size configurable per model profile? Author: added model_profile.chunked_prefill_size and defaulted to 128 tokens.
Liam O'Connor (approval): Verified perf improvements on dedicated canary; approve after CI green.
discussion_thread: Reviewer comments addressed across 3 follow-up commits. Main concerns were safety of overlapping KV access (addressed by epoch checks + debug asserts) and avoiding wasted speculative work (addressed by heuristic gating). We also added metric hooks for rollout monitoring: prefill-chunk-latency, speculative-prefill-hit-rate, overlap-scheduler-decision-rate.
notes_for_cherry_pick: Backport to release/2026-02 required minimal API changes (flags and scheduler shim). Cherry-pick will need KV epoch helper from this branch; keep speculative prefill disabled by default on older branches.
perf_benchmarks: Attached benchmark scripts under examples/benchmarks. Representative numbers: +12% throughput tokens/s on mixed workloads, p95 latency improvement 15-21% depending on seq lengths. Benchmarks captured on A100x8 cluster, model=gpt-70b-ctx32k, batch sizes 1-8.
upgrade_instructions: Enable feature flags via tools/feature_flags/flags.json. For Dedicated customers, coordinate rollout with infra to ensure aux worker pools are available. If p95 increases are observed, disable 'speculative_prefill' flag first.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: speculative prefill could waste GPU cycles for non-decode requests and increase contention. Mitigation: heuristic gating, rollout to canaries, automatic rollback triggers based on latency/error percentiles. Additional risk: race conditions in KV access under overlap; mitigated by epoch checks and debug assertions.
testing_summary: Added unit tests for chunking logic and KV epoch checks; integration perf tests in tests/perf. Ran canary on dedicated pool for 48h with no regressions. Nightly GPU integration passed.
